CZ_NAME: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A large, long period swell impacted the California coastline for two days from December 28-29. A pair of fishermen were killed during the event from a sneaker wave which washed them off the rocks they were fishing on.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A pair of fishermen, father and son, and a friend were fishing on rocks near the Golden Gate Bridge. A large sneaker wave swept them off the rocks and into the ocean. The friend was able to swim back to shore and contacted authorities. A Tiburon Fire Department boat found the bodies of the father and son about 100 yards offshore with the assistance of a Coast Guard Helicopter.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Four people were swept into the ocean at Bonny Doon Beach in Santa Cruz County due to Sneaker Waves. Two men  were rescued by a USCG helicopter. Two women died as a result of drowning.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Four people were swept into the ocean by a sneaker wave at Bonny Doon Beach in Santa Cruz County. Two of the men reached nearby rocks and were rescued by a Coast Guard helicopter. The two women died as a result of drowning.

CZ_NAME: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: On January 1, long period swell from the Pacific created hazardous beach conditions in the area with sneaker waves and large breaking surf.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A visitor to Point Reyes was walking along the beach with his wife and their dog. A wave swept their dog into the ocean, and the man and his wife went into the water after their dog. The wife and dog made it out of the water, but the man did not and was carried out to sea. A coast guard helicopter and life boat found the man's body later that afternoon and he was pronounced dead.

CZ_NAME: COASTAL NORTH BAY INCLUDING POINT REYES NATIONAL SEASHORE
EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High surf and dangerous beach conditions were present during the weekend of October 11-12. Several rescues took place at area beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Two men were fishing on rocks in the Marin Headlands. A sneaker wave swept them off the rocks south of Rodeo Beach and into the Ocean. The Coast Guard, National Park Service, and Southern Marin figherfighters responded. They found one individual clinging to rocks and rescued him and he was treated for hypothermia. One victim was found by a Coast Guard boat in the water, deceased.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: High surf and dangerous beach conditions were present during the weekend of October 11-12. Several rescues took place at area beaches.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Three people were on the beach at Gray Whale Cove when a Sneaker Wave washed them out into the ocean. A dozen beachgoers formed a human chain and pulled the three from the water. Emergency responders performed CPR on a woman pulled from the surf. She was airlifted to a hospital but died. The other two people rescued were treated for hypothermia.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A rogue wave capsized a boat of unknown size near Port Aransas on Saturday morning. The capsizing of the boat resulted when another boat of unknown size crashed into it, possibly causing it to sink. Eight people were rescued from the water by the USCG. An 85-year old male was rushed to the hospital and suffered a severe hip injury and a compound fracture as a result of the incident.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A rogue wave capsized a boat of unknown size near Port Aransas, TX on Saturday morning. The capsizing of the boat resulted in another boat of unknown size crashing into it, possibly causing it to sink. 8 people were rescued from the water by the USCG. An 85-year old male was rushed to the hospital and suffered a severe hip injury and a compound fracture as a result of the incident. United States Coast Guard units from Port Aransas and Corpus Christi along with the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department assisted with incident.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong stationary low pressure system off the British Columbia coast brought impressively high seas into the Oregon Coast. EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A modest swell brought some larger waves to the coast. This was not a large event, nor unusual.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Shelter Cove Fire Department responded to a call about two hikers in the water who had tried to pass a point while hiking The Lost Coast Trail. The tides were not very low this day during the afternoon, nor particularly high, about 4 feet. The swell was around 11 feet at 10 seconds, which brought some larger waves to the Black Sands Beach, though well below advisory criteria. Still, in this particular spot is a steep and dangerous beach. Witnesses described one large wave that washed up farther than any other recent wave causing a hiker to be washed into the rocks. One of the hikers was pronounced dead when rescuers arrived, while the other was injured during an attempted rescue and rushed to the hospital (and did survive).

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A father and son from San Jose perished at Cowell Ranch State Beach near Half Moon Bay after the son was swept into the ocean by a sneaker wave. State park lifeguards and rangers responded to the water rescue and pulled the two into a Harbor Patrol vessel. The two were taken to Stanford Medical Center, where they died. A Beach Hazards Statement was in effect due to an increased risk of sneaker waves and rip currents, especially along west-facing beaches. At the time of the incident, Saildrone 1801593 (at the approximate site of the former buoy 46012 near Half Moon Bay) reported a significant wave height of 6.9 feet and a dominant period of 18 seconds.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A person was knocked off of their feet by a sneaker wave while walking on the beach near the mouth of Siletz Bay. They were then swept out to sea by a rip current.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A person was walking on the sand near the mouth of Siletz Bay when a sneaker wave knocked them off of their feet and dragged them into the ocean.  Once in the water, a strong rip current quickly swept them out to sea. They were swept out far enough that the people on the beach could not see them. The person did not survive, and their body was found on the beach around 4 miles south from where they were swept in. The 3 pm buoy observation from buoy 46050 reported a west swell of 11ft with a 16 second period.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A 32-year old man died after drowning off Bean Hollow State Beach in southern San Mateo County. California State Parks was informed of a possible drowning around 3:25 PM on December 3, when a woman told them that she and her husband were fishing on the rocks, when the woman went to her car and returned to find her husband gone. A bystander saw a body in the water, and Cal Fire retrieved the body and attempted lifesaving measures, which ultimately failed. The man was pronounced dead at the scene. At the time of the incident, wave heights were just under 5ft with a long period swell of 14sec at the San Francisco Bar buoy and a Beach Hazards Statement was in effect.
